name: Bass music - Reusable loud rack
summary: OTT-style density into saturation, then a corrective low cut and a small EQ trim, for a bass patch built from the manual.

device_moves.why: 80% of the OTT amount (Live exposes Amount as 0.0-1.0; the factory default is 1.0), per the recipe manual
5.0 dB of drive: Live exposes Drive as 0.0-1.0 where 0.5 is 0.0 dB, so 0.5694 reads back 5.0 dB
fully wet, as the recipe manual states
band 1 as a 12 dB/octave high pass, so the frequency move really is a low cut
30.0 Hz low cut (Live stores EQ Eight frequency as 0.0-1.0; 0.14275 reads back 30.0 Hz)
small corrective cut on band 2, not a tone move (EQ Eight gain is in dB)

manual.instruction: Print or meter the patch before the rack. Pick a repeatable peak target and compare before/after at matched loudness rather than deciding by the meter alone.
manual.verify: The processed bass is louder but not obviously flatter or more distorted.
manual.why: Dripment builds a saved loud rack and repeatedly A/Bs the gain before and after it.

manual.instruction: Start the chain with OTT around 60 dB and roughly 80% depth, then a Saturator around 5 dB with dry/wet at 100%. Add a second OTT/Saturator stage around 6 dB and 76%.
manual.verify: Each stage adds a little density; no single stage is doing all the work.
manual.why: Dripment's Serum 2 loud rack uses two OTT/Saturator pairs with those starting values.

manual.instruction: Turn off random movement so repeated hits are identical. Adjust OTT amount and depth by ear for each patch instead of copying the same numbers.
manual.verify: The same MIDI note produces the same sound every time.
manual.why: Dripment disables randomness in OTT and changes the amount per sound.

manual.instruction: Finish with EQ Eight for corrective boosts/cuts and a clipper for the final peak. Back off the clipper if the transient starts to flatten.
manual.verify: The bass is competitive in level and still has a discernible attack.
manual.why: Dripment ends the rack with EQ Eight and a clipper.

manual.instruction: Group the devices, save the rack, and reuse it across basses. Resample the processed hit before adding more movement or chopping.
manual.verify: The rack is recallable and the resampled version keeps the same character.
manual.why: Dripment saves the grouped effects as a rack and reuses it on the next bass routine.

manual.instruction: Check the result in mono and against the kick/sub. If the low end disappears or the midrange pinches, bypass stages and rebuild one at a time.
manual.verify: The loudness survives mono and the kick still reads.
manual.why: A loud rack can hide phase and low-end problems; the tutorials repeatedly check the sound in context rather than soloed.
